summary: Cross-account permission surface mismatch prevents service-account impersonation in prod
description: Internal ML engineer can impersonate the staging service account but receives permission errors when attempting to impersonate the prod service account during model promotion. This blocks Dedicated capacity smoke tests and a release gating job.
impact: Engineering cannot run cross-account model promotion jobs in prod; blocks Dedicated capacity smoke tests and delays release by estimated 48+ hours if not resolved.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) From infra-dev workstation with dev creds, run: aws sts assume-role --role-arn arn:aws:iam::PROD_ACCOUNT:role/redwood-deploy-proxy --role-session-name test
2) Observe success in staging. Repeat with production project: gcloud iam service-accounts impersonate redwood-prod-sa@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com --resulting error.
3) Run bake job: ./scripts/promote_model.sh --env prod --model v1.2.3
4) Job fails within 10s with 'Permission denied' from KMS and '403: Service account iam.serviceAccounts.get' in GCP stack.
logs:
aws sts assume-role error: 'User: arn:aws:sts::111111111111:assumed-role/infra-developer is not authorized to perform: sts:AssumeRole on resource arn:aws:iam::222222222222:role/redwood-deploy-proxy'
gcloud error: 'PERMISSION_DENIED: Service account redwood-prod-sa@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com: The caller does not have permission iam.serviceAccounts.get'
Audit entry: PROD project denies via org-policy constraint: constraints/iam.allowedPolicyMemberDomains with unexpected domain mapping.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: trust relationship or role binding differs between staging and prod. Checked aws trust policy for redwood-deploy-proxy in prod; trust includes principal infra-deploy@redwood.io but missing federated identity used by CI runner. GCP IAM shows iam.serviceAccountUser binding exists for staging CI group but not for prod CI group. Org policy on prod project enforces domain-limited members which rejects the service account impersonation from our external CI token exchange. Found conditional binding on prod requiring 'request.time' tag for JIT sessions (added Sep 2025) not present in dev flows. Confirmed terraform drift: prod binding was created manually during emergency in 2025 and not codified.
proposed_workaround:
1) Grant iam.serviceAccountUser to infra-temp-ci@redwood.io in prod via JIT for 4 hours.
2) Run promotion from a prod-network bastion with elevated session as short term. Both require security approval and oncall coordination.
actions_taken: Opened #sec-access conversation and requested JIT elevation. Created WIP PR to codify missing binding: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/2987. Notified oncall SRE to prepare audit logs and monitor promotion job.
resolution_notes: Temporary binding approved and applied on 2026-03-04 22:10 UTC; promotion job retried and succeeded at 22:34 UTC. Long-term fix: codify prod binding in terraform, remove manual conditional mismatch, and add CI integration test to catch drift. No customer impact reported.
